review_notes: I read the whole file and searched Mathlib/Condensed/Light for uses of the `_apply` lemmas and `coverToFun`. The only simp-tagged lemmas are `mem_fibres_iff` and `mem_S'_iff`, and both look fine. `mem_fibres_iff` rewrites a membership statement into its characterisation, so it cannot loop. `mem_S'_iff` is `Iff.rfl`. The `@[simps! pt ι_app]` on `cocone` is used by an explicit `simp only`, and I found no problem with it. The findings are about the interface of the plain `def`s (`π_r`, `fibreIncl`, `y`, `coverToFun`). Each has an `_apply` equation that is `grind`-only, or is in a non-canonical form. I did not run Lean, so I claim no observed simp failures, only that these defs are opaque to simp and the lemmas are not simp-visible. Whether adding `@[simp]` would change the later large `simp` calls is uncertain.

findings.excerpt:
coverToFun i π t =
      Sum.elim (fun t ↦ ⟨(t, t), rfl⟩) (fun xy ↦ ⟨(i xy.val.1, i xy.val.2), xy.prop⟩) t
findings.problem: This equation is just the unfolded definition. Its right-hand side is `Sum.elim … t` for an arbitrary `t`, and it restates the whole body of `coverToFun`. It is not a usable simp lemma: if tagged it would only expand the definition into a `Sum.elim` application that still has to be reduced. It is tagged `grind =` only. The real simp-normal forms are on the two constructors, and these are missing. The one downstream simp-style use, `dsimp [coverToFun]` in `cover`, has to unfold the definition.
findings.proposed_change: Replace the single unfolding lemma with constructor-specific equations, e.g. `coverToFun_inl : coverToFun i π (Sum.inl t) = ⟨(t, t), rfl⟩` and `coverToFun_inr : coverToFun i π (Sum.inr xy) = ⟨(i xy.val.1, i xy.val.2), xy.prop⟩`. Tag both `@[simp, grind =]`. Both are `rfl` and terminate. Keep the general `_apply` lemma, if at all, only as a non-simp lemma.
findings.benefit: Anyone using `coverToFun i π (Sum.inl _)` or `(Sum.inr _)` gets the canonical simp normal form without unfolding the definition. This matches how `Sum.elim` is normally handled and avoids a `dsimp [coverToFun]` or `rfl` unfolding.

findings.excerpt:
@[grind =]
lemma π_r_apply (π : T → S × Option X) (σ : Option X → S → T)
    (x : fibres π σ) : π_r π σ x = π x :=
  rfl
findings.problem: `π_r`, `fibreIncl` and `y` are ordinary (irreducible-to-simp) defs. Their only characterising equations, `π_r_apply`, `fibreIncl_apply` and `y_apply` (line 158–159), are tagged `grind =` but not `simp`. The sibling lemmas `mem_fibres_iff` and `mem_S'_iff` are tagged `simp`. Because of this, `simp` cannot see through these projections. Proofs such as `sectionOfFibreIncl` and `coverToFun_surjective` have to be done by `grind`, and the file's `simp` calls (e.g. line 110 `by simp`, and the `simp` calls in `aux`) cannot rewrite `π_r π σ x` or `fibreIncl π σ x` to the underlying `π x` and `x`. The interface is therefore inconsistent: the same equations work for `grind` but not for `simp`.
findings.proposed_change: Tag the pure projection equations `@[simp, grind =]`: `π_r_apply`, `fibreIncl_apply`, and `y_apply`. The left sides are the applied defs and the right sides are strictly simpler terms (`π x`, `↑x`, `(π (x.val ∞).val).1`), so there is no loop and no competing rule. If the maintainers want to avoid changing behaviour in the large `simp` calls, at least `π_r_apply` and `fibreIncl_apply` should be simp.
findings.benefit: The normal form `π x` / `x` becomes available to `simp` and `simp_all`. Goals about `Prod.snd ∘ π_r π σ` and `fibreIncl π σ x` can then be closed without switching to `grind`. This keeps the simp and grind interfaces aligned.

evidence.excerpt: lemma y_apply (π : T → S × OnePoint X) (x : S' π) : y π x = (π (x.val ∞).val).1 := rfl

lemma fibreIncl_apply (π : T → S × Option X) (σ : Option X → S → T)
    (x : (Prod.snd ∘ π_r π σ) ⁻¹' {none}) : fibreIncl π σ x = x
